precepts.text: In the place where it was said unto them, ye are not my people, there it shall be said, ye are the sons of the living God. Where we were made dysfunctional and called coon and spear-chucker, everything except Israelites, the Lord will beautify the meek. The nations that put their hands on the apple of his eye will pay; he allows it and still makes them pay.
precepts.point: An everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him; he goes out of Zion with a rod of iron and it will hurt. Hitherto is the end of the matter: God's whole plan is Israel ruling this planet indefinitely with every other dominion serving the Most High through her. Point blank, full stop.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

The place where it was said, ye are not my people, is the place where we were made to be dysfunctional, where we were made a mess, where they called us coon and spear-chucker. They called us everything except the Israelites. In that very place the Most High is going to beautify the meek with salvation, and there it shall be said, ye are the sons of the living God. That is Daniel 7:27: the kingdom under the whole heaven given “to the people of the saints of the most High”.

The Lord is going to punish the nations for what they called us and did to us, because we are God's heritage. Those who put their nasty, mangy hands on us touched the apple of his eye, and they are going to pay for it. Our brothers and sisters were hung and suffered all kinds of evil, and the Most High has the chart on everything. The Lord allowed it to happen, and he is still going to make them pay for doing it.

precepts.text: In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people. This is where they destroyed our nationality, called us out of our name, called us undocumented workers, and when we try to pick up the Bible and gain our nationality back they label it a hate crime, because they propagated a set of people and said these are the Jews. That is why Psalms 83 says they have consulted that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. There it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God: that is what is happening to you, brothers and sisters, right here in Babylon the Great, which means they cannot stop this gospel. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head: that is Christ, and they shall come up out of the land. That is when we go home.
precepts.point: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God. The wilderness is Africa; we fled out of Jerusalem into Africa, the same place where Joseph took the young child and his mother. Then a place was prepared, which is the Americas. A thousand two hundred and threescore days: 1260 days, three and a half, the same period written as forty and two months and as a time, times, and the dividing of time in Daniel 7 and 8.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God.” The wilderness is Africa, where we fled out of Jerusalem. After the wilderness we came to a place, and Hosea tells what that place is: “it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

This is where they destroyed our nationality, in the Americas. The place where it was said, you are not the Israelites. They called us out of our name; they called us undocumented workers. And when we pick up the Bible to gain our nationality back, they label it a hate crime, because they propagated a set of people and said these are the Jews. That is why Psalms 83 says they have consulted that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.

“there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” That is what is happening to you, brothers and sisters, right here in Babylon the Great, in the place prepared for the woman. It means they cannot stop this gospel.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”: that one head is Christ. “and they shall come up out of the land”: that is when we go home.

precepts.text: Call her name Loruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel. They fully went into idolatry. Call his name Loammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God. That was the message to the northern kingdom because of their idolatry. But then it comes back: in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again. All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to repent: if there were no endgame where we come out of this, there is no incentive.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Hosea shows why Ephraim was let alone. “Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” He would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, because they fully went into idolatry. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen”, as can be read in 2 Kings 19.

“Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” That was the message to the northern kingdom because of his anger at their idolatry: you will not be my people, and I will not be your God. That is why the woman said the Jews have no dealings with us.

But then it comes back: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again.

All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to change and repent. If there were no endgame where we come out of this, there would be no incentive. But God said if you turn back to me, in the place where it was said you are not my people, there you will be called the sons of God.

precepts.text: Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head. In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. The time has come, Peter: we have to gather them together. And guess what: that is happening now. It has been going on since back then until now: we are out in South America gathering God's people, out in Africa gathering God's people, here in the States bringing God's people back together.
precepts.point: Take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah; then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim. This is what Peter would have had to read to them, to convince them that the cleansing of the northern kingdom was going to happen and they would be brought back in.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
When the voice told Peter, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common”, Peter would have had to go to the Old Testament to explain what God had cleansed. He would go to Ezekiel 37: “I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” And whom was he gathering, and from where? “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”: they were living among the Gentiles, the nations. He gathers them, cleanses them, and takes the two kingdoms, the stick of Judah and the stick of Joseph in the hand of Ephraim, and makes them one.

Hosea shows the same joining: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” That is the two sticks becoming one in the Lord's hand.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The northern kingdom, cast out among the heathen and called not my people, would be called the sons of the living God again. That was the prophecy, and that is why Peter could not call those men common: the time had come, Peter, we have to gather them together, bring them together.

And guess what: that is happening now. It has been going on since back then until now. We are out in South America gathering God's people, out in Africa gathering God's people, and here in the States bringing God's people back together, Judah and Israel under one head.

precepts.text: In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people: in America and the diaspora, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Europe. There it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: After the Most High sent the flood, those same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The title “sons of God” runs through the whole book. After Deuteronomy called Israel “the children of the Lord your God,” did anything change in the prophets? No. Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people.” That place is where our people are today: America and the diaspora, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Europe. Everywhere we were told we are not God’s people. “there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

God calls us the sons of the living God. That is who we are. So the sons of God of Genesis 6 are the same nation the prophet speaks of: the children of Israel, scattered and counted as nothing, yet still his sons. The world does not know us, but God does, and in the very place where we were called not his people, he will call us his sons again.

precepts.text: The historian Duran found confirmation in the promise that the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea: surely, he argued, this promise was fulfilled by the multitudes the Spanish found in the new world. He also noted the traditions of long journeys like the one from Assyria to Arzareth, traditions of flights like the Exodus from Egypt, manna falling from heaven, and an old man who began the tale of his people's origins with the words in the beginning, roughly parallel to Genesis. Why would so-called Indians be quoting the Bible unless they were Israelites?
precepts.point: Book read in class, Lost Tribes and Promised Lands by Ronald Sanders (1978): Columbus gave to the peaceable multitude of the islands the name Indios, because he considered their habitation to be the Indies, but perhaps also because he thought of them as living in God, en Dios. Columbus was reading the book of Esdras. The scriptures call them a peaceable multitude; the world called them noble savages.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

precepts.why:
“Afterward saw I the same man come down from the mountain, and call unto him another peaceable Multitude.” The same man is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah of Revelation 1, with feet like burnt brass and hair like wool. And the angel explains it: “he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him”, those are the ten tribes, the northern kingdom. That is who Christ gathers in these last days, through the work the prophets are doing in the worldwide blitzes, in Puerto Rico, Ecuador, Mexico, Chile.

The historians knew who that peaceable multitude was. Columbus gave the peaceable multitude of the islands the name Indios, because he took their home to be the Indies, but perhaps also because he thought of them as living in God, en Dios. Columbus was reading the book of Esdras. The scriptures call them a peaceable multitude; the world called them noble savages.

The historian Duran found more confirmation in Hosea: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.” Surely, he argued, that promise was fulfilled by the multitudes the Spanish found in the new world. Remember Israel blessed Ephraim and Manasseh to be a multitude of nations; that is what the Spaniards found.

Duran also noted that the Indians of Mexico had traditions of long journeys like the one from Assyria to Arzareth, flights like the Exodus from Egypt, earthquakes that swallowed evil men, manna falling from heaven, and an old man who began the tale of his people’s origins with the words in the beginning, like Genesis. Why would so-called Indians be quoting the Bible unless they were Israelites? We had books, we carried the Bible with us, and they stole our records.

So the peaceable multitude Christ calls is the ten tribes scattered on this side of the world, and Hosea’s promise stands over them: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

precepts.text: The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea which cannot be numbered, and where it was said ye are not my people they shall be called the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: These are they which came out of great tribulation and washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb: so much for not going through tribulation.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number”. Now that we are bringing this out, the churches say we are all included, all backgrounds and cultures together. Where was that in 1964? Where was it on the slave ships? That is why the Bible says precept must be upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little.

Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. That is us. The multitude “which no man could number” is the children of Israel, whose number cannot be measured nor numbered.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people told they were not God’s people are the same ones called the sons of the living God.

It also shows time has gone by. Moses said “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”, because they were killing us; Hosea says we would grow to be like the sand of the sea. That is the great multitude standing before the throne.

precepts.text: I will make them one nation upon the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king to them all; they shall be no more two nations, neither divided into two kingdoms any more.
precepts.point: Yet in the place where it was said, Ye are not my people, it shall be said, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah, the nation, and the children of Israel, the company of nations, be gathered together and appoint themselves one head, Christ.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Hosea says, “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”. The children of Judah are the nation; the children of Israel, the northern kingdom, are the company of nations. Gathered together means they become one, and the one head is Christ. You read the same thing from multiple prophets, and Ezekiel says it this way: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all”. The one king is the one head.

“and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”: no more southern and northern. Remember, one of them was not a nation at all. Isaiah said, “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” Ephraim became Lo-ammi, not my people, Gentiles, heathen, uncircumcised, all the same. “Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things”. They are brought back together, just as Hosea said.

Christ said the same out of his own mouth: “I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”. This fold is Judah, because Christ is of Judah; the other sheep are the northern kingdom. “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice”: they hear through the teachings of Judah first. “and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” The one shepherd is Christ himself. He is quoting Hosea 1:10-11 and Ezekiel 37:22.

Even Caiaphas, who hated the Messiah, prophesied it: “that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Those scattered abroad are the strangers of 1 Peter 1, the northern kingdom. The builders were appointed to reject Christ so he would be killed, and by his death the northern kingdom would get the chance to repent and be redeemed back into the fold. That could not be done unless Christ died.

So the not my people of Hosea 1 are the strangers Peter wrote to, “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”. Christ gathers both kingdoms together as one nation under one king.

precepts.text: In the place where it was said, ye are not my people, it shall be said, ye are the sons of the living God, and Judah and Israel shall be gathered under one head.
precepts.point: A people God disowns are Gentiles and strangers. Judah read this and treated the northern tribes as Gentiles from then on.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Hosea's children were for signs. His daughter Lo-ruhamah means no mercy: “I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away”, which is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim so that it would be not a people. Then his son: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” When you are not God's people and he is not your God, what does that make you? A Gentile, a heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. Judah read this and said, good, the hell with Ephraim; they ain't his people no more, they're Gentiles, and we can't deal with them.

But Hosea goes straight on: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” When they were told they were Gentiles, it would be said to them, no, you are not Gentiles; you are God's people.

Judah forgot this. Judah said, you guys are Gentiles forever. But Hosea says eventually you have to come together again: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”. That one head is Christ, and they are delivered together, united as one. Chapter 2 says the same: “I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” Judah just took a black highlighter and covered that part, because they were evil and stupid.

The same thing is in Chronicles. The northern kingdom was “without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law”, because Jeroboam set up idols in Dan and Shiloh so they would not go south to worship in Jerusalem. That is why they were called strangers: King Asa “gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” Whenever Judah was on point, Ephraim came in. The Lord always uses Judah to bring Ephraim back, and the strangers, the not my people, turn out to be the sons of the living God.

precepts.point: This is not a time of peace but of war; not physical war, but uniting, keeping the law and waiting on the Redeemer.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel shall be “as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”: dispersed, so that we could be preserved. And “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” We are hearing that now and seeing it now. Our teachers tell us these things, we identify with them, and that is how we regain our identity.

Solomon’s prayer shows the steps: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

First we have to bethink ourselves: remember ourselves and reclaim our identity, right here in the land of our captivity. That is part of the strangeness of our salvation. Then we repent and make supplication, and then God will acknowledge us, be for us and fight for us.

This is not a time of peace but a time of war. Not physical war: there is nothing we can do against these powers and nations physically. What we can do is unite as a people, come back together, keep God’s laws in solidarity, and wait on our Redeemer. In the place where we were called not his people, we remember who we are, we repent, and we are called the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.
precepts.point: This is not a time of peace but of war; not physical war, but uniting, keeping the law and waiting on the Redeemer.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
How do we bring about that change? How do you fight a nuke? How do you fight powers that can turn off your lights, run your economy and take your resources right under your nose while you say thank you? With something small and simple: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

It was God’s wisdom that the world would not know him, that they would purposely not be able to understand. It is given unto us to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; he made everything a mystery so that only his elect can unseal what the Bible says. And just as it pleases him to see a man lifted up in power so that he can take him down, it pleases him to save by the foolishness of preaching. That is how we get our identity back. That is how we come back.

So look at the brothers in the streets. Don’t think those efforts are small; they are making an impact. Even if your camp doesn’t have a lot of foot traffic, none of it is in vain, none of it is void. You go out, you preach, you gather, you fish. Even if there are scarce fish in that water, if you know there is a spot where fish be, you stay there until you catch at least one. You are not trying to come home empty.

It starts with preaching and then it escalates. First we repent, then we get the honor. We do not fight physically now: we repent now, we fight through preaching, and God fights for us later. Then comes the honor of Psalm 149, “a twoedged sword in their hand; To execute vengeance upon the heathen”, for “this honour have all his saints.” When he shall roar, “the children shall tremble from the west”, the western hemisphere, “and I will place them in their houses, saith the Lord”: our tribes, our royal heritage and our identity given back to us, the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea; they shall be called the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: This is the same covenant language spoken over the children of Israel: as the sand of the sea which cannot be measured nor numbered.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
“I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed also be numbered.” That is covenant language, and it is the same language spoken over the children of Israel: “the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

The seed of Abram that cannot be numbered is the children of Israel. And Hosea says where that seed ends up: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The promise to Abram’s seed as the dust of the earth is the promise to Israel, the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea; that is the dust of Jacob no man can count.
precepts.point: Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his. The last end of Israel is a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord: the land married, double for our shame, everlasting joy, and a seed acknowledged among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. That is why we cannot wait for those days.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
“Who can count the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel?” No man can. “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

Israel is as the sand of the sea; that is the dust of Jacob no man can count. And Hosea says where it ends: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people that shall dwell alone and not be reckoned among the nations are the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: Ye are not my people; yet in the place where that was said, it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, that provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? That was the nation which was not a people, our own brothers and sisters broken off for a dispensation of time.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
Hosea says it of the northern kingdom: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” There are those which are not a people. “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

That is how the Most High moves Judah to jealousy with those which are not a people, and provokes them to anger with a foolish nation. The northern kingdom was cut off for over six hundred years while Judah kept the priesthood and the sacrifices. When Christ's apostles were sent to the northern kingdom and brought them back into the fold, it provoked Judah to jealousy: we put in all this work with Ezra and Zerubbabel and the Maccabees, and all of a sudden they get to come back home? The nation which was not a people was our own brothers and sisters, broken off for a dispensation of time, and now called the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen; prophecy that Judah would be saved without carnal weapons.
precepts.point: All this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's. The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
The Lord said it long before: “I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.” That is a prophecy that Judah would be saved without carnal weapons.

David spoke the same thing to Goliath's face: “the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s.” He prophesied the outcome before the fight, “This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand”, so “that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.”

The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done. Judah is saved “by the Lord their God”, not by bow or by sword.

precepts.text: The children of Judah and Israel shall be gathered together under one head and come up out of the land.
precepts.point: The northern and southern kingdoms are to be made one nation again under one king and one shepherd. The one king is Jesus Christ, called the throne of David because David ruled over all twelve tribes; David will be present but is not the king. The chief shepherd, the great shepherd, the good shepherd who lays down his life is Christ, and he gathers the elect from the four winds and brings them up out of the land.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land.”

The children of Judah, the southern kingdom, and the children of Israel, the northern kingdom, are gathered together under one head, and that head is Christ. David said, “thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel to be a people unto thee for ever.” The same people he redeemed from Egypt he gathers again and brings up out of the land.

precepts.text: The Most High names Jezreel to declare He will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu.
precepts.point: Names in this line carry meaning, as when the Most High named the children of Hosea to declare His judgment on the house of Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.” The Most High named the child Jezreel to declare His judgment.

Names in the line of Jerahmeel carry meaning the same way. The record names his sons through his wives, Ram, Onam, Shammai, Jada and the rest, and keeps account even of the branches that did not continue: “Seled died without children”, and “Jether died without children.”

precepts.text: The Most High names Lo-ruhamah, for He will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel.
precepts.point: Names in this line carry meaning, as when the Most High named the children of Hosea to declare His judgment on the house of Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And God said unto him, Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” The Most High named her Lo-ruhamah, for He would no more have mercy upon the house of Israel.

The name itself declares the judgment. That is how names carry meaning in scripture, and why the names in this line of Judah are set down one by one.

precepts.text: The Most High will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel but will utterly take them away, and calls them Loammi, "not my people."
precepts.point: Isaiah then prophesied that because Ephraim conspired with Syria, Ephraim would be broken within sixty-five years so that it would be "not a people," and Hosea said the same, that Ephraim was joined to idols and would get no more mercy but be utterly taken away and carried into Assyria. Broken and removed from the land, they lost their nationality, culture, and heritage and were assimilated into the nations.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Hosea said the same. “Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away. But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah.”

Then: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” The house of Israel, the northern kingdom, would get no more mercy and would be utterly taken away, and they were called not my people. That is why they were counted as one of another nation.

precepts.text: In the place where it was said "ye are not my people," there they shall be called the sons of the living God.
precepts.point: The restoration is two sticks made one nation. Ephraim, once "not a people," is called back and named the sons of the living God, having obtained mercy that they had not obtained, so the Gentiles being brought in are the outcasts of Israel that Christ came to be a light to.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

Ephraim, once Lo-ammi, “not a people”, is called back and named the sons of the living God. The same house of Israel that was broken and taken away is restored in the very place where it was called not my people.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why:
This is our deliverance, what the churches call the rapture; the word rapture is Latin for caught up, taken up. The article quoted this as Hosea 2:2; it is Hosea 1:11. Read the verse before it: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered;” I don't care what their census says; God says we number the sand of the sea. We are the largest nation on the planet earth. “and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” That is evidence that the real Israelites would lose their identity and gain it back in the last days. That is super heavy; where does that apply to these so-called Jews? Nowhere. That fits us. You see in the scriptures where it says ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake: nobody cares what is in the Quran, or the isms; all the nonsense in the Talmud, all that filth we just read, no big deal; but when we read things out of the Bible, all of a sudden it is an issue. Brothers and sisters, welcome to the truth; this is why we are fighting right now.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head,” That is Christ. “and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” So the deliverance is only for Judah and Israel, the two kingdoms. It is not for Baptists or Catholics or Mormons or Muslims; it is for the Israelites, Judah and Israel.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 12 Red Dragon, Red Herring

precepts.why: What is the place prepared of God? “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God”: this place is America. The teaching started here in the United States of America, not in Africa, the UK or the Caribbean islands.
